prompt:
Research the officially documented limits of a free Gmail / Google account: total storage, attachment size for sending and receiving, recipients per day. Cite Google's own help pages and quote the limits.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Here are the officially documented limits for a free Gmail / Google account, based on Google's own help pages.

SOURCE: https://support.google.com/mail/answer/9312312 | QUOTE: "Each Google Account includes up to 15 GB of storage, which is shared across Gmail, Google Drive, and Google Photos." | CLAIM: Total storage for a free Google account is 15 GB.

SOURCE: https://support.google.com/mail/answer/6584 | QUOTE: "For personal Gmail accounts, the limit is 25 MB." | CLAIM: The attachment size limit for sending in a free personal Gmail account is 25 MB.

SOURCE: https://support.google.com/mail/answer/22839 | QUOTE: "500 recipients in a single email and or more than 500 emails sent in a day." | CLAIM: The sending limit for a free Gmail account is 500 recipients per single email and a maximum of 500 emails sent per day.

SOURCE: https://support.google.com/a/answer/1366776 | QUOTE: "You can receive emails of up to 50 MB (Enterprise Standard) or 70 MB (Enterprise Plus)*." | CLAIM: The documented receiving size limit of 50 MB to 70 MB applies to Google Workspace Enterprise editions, not free personal accounts.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: The official receiving email size limit for a free, personal Gmail account.
